newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Namibian leader invites Singaporean investors.
newsitem.headline: Namibian leader invites Singaporean investors.

text.p: Namibian President Sam Nujoma invited Singaporean businessmen on Monday to invest in his country and said Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong will probably visit its capital, Windhoek, next year.
"We're interested in trading and inviting members of the business community in Singapore to invest in Namibia," Nujoma told reporters in a briefing here.
Nujoma said a technical mission from Singapore will fly to his country in January to train Namibians in science and math.
"Later on, the Prime Minister will come with a larger business delegation," he said, adding Goh will probably arrive in the first week of March.
Nujoma arrived in Singapore on October 31. He is due to leave for home on Tuesday.

Singapore's trade authority has said it hopes to widen the city-state's access to southern African markets through the Southern African Customs Union, which imposes a standardised tariff system for all imports to member countries.
The union groups Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Botswana and Lesotho.
